queseq8-nature#125.en: False — restrictions from the ORIGINAL equation stand. A value that breaks them is rejected (N.A.), exactly like a rejected x.

queseq8-nature#126.en: The restriction comes from the ORIGINAL equation, before any working started

queseq8-nature#127.en: The algebra cannot un-ban a value — it only shows which values would have solved the changed equation

queseq8-nature#128.en: ∴ false — a parameter that breaks a restriction is rejected as N.A., exactly like a rejected x

queseq8-nature#131.en: Equal roots demand Δ = 0, which gives k(${inner}) = 0, so k = 0 or k = ${C(other)}. But the ORIGINAL equation had kx in a denominator. Final answer?

queseq8-nature#136.en: Check every parameter answer against the original equation's restrictions.

queseq8-nature#137.en: kx in a denominator means k ≠ 0 from the start (and at k = 0 the equation isn't even a quadratic). Reject k = 0: the answer is k = ${C(other)} only.

queseq8-nature#138.en: The algebra gives two candidates: k = 0 or k = ${C(other)}

queseq8-nature#139.en: Now check them against the original equation: kx sat in a denominator, so k ≠ 0 from the very start

queseq8-nature#140.en: k = 0 breaks that restriction, so it is N.A.

queseq8-nature#141.en: at k = 0 the equation is not even a quadratic any more

queseq8-nature#147.en: A power with a positive base can never be negative — the statement can NEVER be true: no solution.

queseq8-nature#149.en: Division by 0 is undefined — the ghost under the bed. Find it by setting the denominator = 0.

queseq8-nature#150.en: A negative under an even root has no real value → non-real. Find it by setting the inside of the root < 0.

queseq8-nature#151.en: An answer from a surd equation that FAILS the test in the original equation

queseq8-nature#152.en: Squaring can invent extra answers. A candidate that fails the original equation is rejected: N.A.

queseq8-nature#153.en: An answer that equals one of the fraction equation's restrictions

queseq8-nature#154.en: The value itself is rejected — mark it N.A. and keep only the valid answer(s).

queseq8-nature#155.en:
KNOW THE DIFFERENCE: which word describes this?
${it.case}

queseq8-nature#156.en: No solution = never true. Undefined = denominator 0. Non-real = negative under √. N.A. = a rejected candidate answer.

queseq8-nature#157.en: Run the four words in order and see which one this case actually fits

queseq8-nature#158.en: No solution = the statement can never be true · undefined = a denominator hits 0 · non-real = a negative sits under an even root · N.A. = a candidate answer that fails the original

queseq8-nature#159.en: the four are not interchangeable — she gives this its own titled box

queseq8-nature#166.en: Undefined is about the BOTTOM: set the denominator equal to 0.

queseq8-nature#167.en: Undefined = denominator 0: x + ${C(m)} = 0 → x = −${C(m)}. (x < −${C(n)} is where it's NON-real — a different question!)

queseq8-nature#168.en: Undefined has one cause only: dividing by 0 — the ghost under the bed

queseq8-nature#169.en: So look at the BOTTOM and set it to 0: x + ${C(m)} = 0

queseq8-nature#171.en: the root is a different question — that one gives NON-real, at x < −${C(n)}

queseq8-nature#173.en: x < −${C(n)} (the inside of the root is negative)

queseq8-nature#176.en: Non-real is about the ROOT: set what's under it less than 0.

queseq8-nature#177.en: Non-real = negative inside the root: x + ${C(n)} < 0 → x < −${C(n)}. (x = −${C(m)} is where it's UNDEFINED — a different question!)

queseq8-nature#178.en: Non-real has one cause only: a negative sitting under an even root

queseq8-nature#179.en: So look INSIDE the root and make it negative: x + ${C(n)} < 0

queseq8-nature#181.en: the denominator is a different question — that one gives UNDEFINED, at x = −${C(m)}
